discourse_text: Some schools make students wear uniforms, and I think this is a good idea.
Uniforms reduce distractions because students no longer compete over expensive clothes.
For example, a 2019 survey of 400 teachers found that 62 percent saw fewer classroom conflicts after a uniform policy began.
Some people argue that uniforms limit self-expression.
However, students can still show personality through hobbies, friendships, and accessories that fit the rules.
In conclusion, uniforms help schools stay focused and fair.
Homework is bad and schools should stop it.
Students get tired and stressed when they have too much homework every night.
My cousin has a lot of homework and it is bad for him.
Teachers might say homework helps students practice what they learned.
But practice can happen in class where the teacher can give help right away.
So homework should be stopped.
Online education is better because it is easy.
Students can choose when to study, which helps those who also have jobs or family duties.
According to a 2020 report by a national education agency, about one third of college students worked at least 20 hours a week.
Critics say online learning makes students feel isolated.
Video calls and discussion boards let learners meet classmates, so isolation can be reduced with good course design.
Overall, online education gives flexibility that many students need.
Have you ever counted how many hours you spend on your phone each day?
Social media should be limited for teenagers.
Too much screen time cuts into sleep, and tired students do worse on tests.
Research from sleep clinics, such as a study of 1,200 teens, links late-night phone use to shorter sleep.
Social media is a thing that is not good for people.
To sum up, parents and schools should set clear time limits.
Cities must make recycling mandatory.
Mandatory recycling lowers the amount of waste that ends up in landfills.
In Seattle, the recycling rate rose from 38 percent to over 50 percent after the city required it.
Others believe that mandatory rules are too costly for small towns.
Yet the savings from smaller landfills can pay back the cost over time, since less waste means lower disposal fees.
Therefore, mandatory recycling is a wise choice for every city.
Schools should start later in the morning.
Teenagers need more sleep, and early starts make it hard to get enough.
Everyone knows that sleeping is good.
Some parents worry that later starts will disrupt work schedules.
Schools could offer supervised morning programs, which would help families who need early drop-off.
In conclusion, a later start would help students learn better.
